{{Short description|German physicist (1926–2010)}}
'''Hans H. Joos''' (31 December 1926, [[Stuttgart]]<ref name=WerWer>{{cite book|editor=Habel, Walter|title=Wer ist wer? Das deutsche Who's who|edition=24|publisher=Schmidt-Römhild|location=Lübeck|year=1985|isbn=3-7950-2005-0|page=588|chapter=Joos, Hans}}</ref> – 18 November 2010, [[Hamburg]]) was a German theoretical physicist.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hpk.uni-hamburg.de/resolve/id/cph_person_00001300 |title=Joos, Hans @ HPK |website=[[Universität Hamburg]] |date=9 July 2018 }}</ref> He is known for the [[Joos–Weinberg equation]],<ref>{{cite journal|last=Joos|first=Hans|date=1962|title=Zur Darstellungstheorie der inhomogenen Lorentzgruppe als Grundlage quantenmechanischer Kinematik|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/prop.2180100302|journal=Fortschritte der Physik|language=German|volume=10|issue=3|pages=65–146|doi=10.1002/prop.2180100302|bibcode=1962ForPh..10...65J |url-access=subscription}}</ref> independently published by [[Steven Weinberg]].

==Education and career==
Joos studied at the [[University of Tübingen]], where he was mentored by [[Gert Molière]] (1909–1964). After graduation, Joos worked in [[São Paulo]] and at the [[University of Hamburg]], where he received his doctorate ([[Promotion (Germany)|''Promotion'']]) in 1961.<ref name=WerWer/> As a postdoc he worked in at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey|Princeton]] (for the academic year 1961–1962),<ref>{{cite web|title=Hans H. Joos|website=Institute for Advanced Study|date=9 December 2019 |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/hans-h-joos}}</ref> at the [[University of Minnesota]], and at [[CERN]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Joos |first1=H. |last2=Weimar |first2=E. |year=1976 |title=On the covariant description of spontaneously broken symmetry in general field theory |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF02730117 |journal=Il Nuovo Cimento A |language=en |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=283–312 |doi=10.1007/BF02730117 |bibcode=1976NCimA..32..283J |issn=0369-3546|url-access=subscription }}</ref> From 1963 until his retirement, he was a member of the scientific research team at Germany's national research centre [[DESY|''Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron'' (DESY)]] in Hamburg and was for some years the head of DESY's theory group. In 1965 he was appointed [[Academic ranks in Germany|''Honorarprofessor'']] of theoretical physics at the University of Hamburg. He served on the editorial board of ''[[Communications in Mathematical Physics]]''. He lived in [[Halstenbek]] (on the north-western border of Hamburg).<ref name=WerWer/>
